sources: Spence, Lewis. The Minor Traditions of British Mythology. New York: Benjamin Blom, Inc., 1972, 96.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Tregeagle is a figure of Cornish folklore. Legend says he was an evil man who killed his wife and pledged his soul to the Devil. He outwitted his fate. He was so selfish that he would not leave earth after death. He stayed on to trouble neighbors who wished to use his land. A local clergyman tried to save his soul. He set Tregeagle to empty a pool with a seashell. Tregeagle worked until he grew weary. The moment he stopped to rest, the Devil came and dragged him away. The Cornish still say a loud noise roars like Tregeagle.
